source_title: oneo-me/nsgo: A cross-platform native UI engine with a Go backend: write apps in Go with signals, memos and flexbox layout, and each platform draws with its own native views — iOS, macOS, Windows, Android, Linux and the web - GitHub
source_excerpt:
NSGo is a cross-platform native UI engine with a Go backend. App logic, the reactive graph and layout run in Go, and each platform draws with its own native UI.
NSGo follows the design of Native Shell (NSH) , which does the same in Rust. It exists for teams that want NSH's model without writing Rust.
NSGo is early. It has NSH's reactive model, layout, text, images, canvas, shaders, animations, services and unstyled base components on macOS, iOS, Windows, Linux, the web and Android, and apps embed in iOS, Android and Go desktop apps of their own. There is no release or stable API yet. ARCHITECTURE.md tracks each target.
Write apps and components in Go, with signals, memos and effects.
Lay out with flexbox and grid, and render with each platform's own views and text.
Target iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux and the web, as NSH does.
Embed NSGo apps in existing native apps, or package them as standalone apps.
An app is a Go main package that calls nsgo.Run . Components are functions or types that return elements; signals update what reads them:
Test it headless with nsgotest , no window needed; go tool nsgo test -target macos runs the same tests in a real window, with native input and screenshots ( app.Screenshot("name") ):
An app can also be written in TSX, as an NSH app is with its imports naming nsgo , and styled with Tailwind CSS classes: the package embeds its sources, which the tool compiles ahead into its builds, and go run and go test compile as the app starts, with no Node. examples/tsx is one.
TSX imports base 's components from nsgo/base , and an app's own Go components once it registers them: tsx.Register("app/native", map[string]core.Node{"Badge": Badge{}}) makes import { Badge } from "app/native" take Badge 's fields as props. A tsconfig.json extending .nsgo/tsconfig.json lets go tool nsgo check vet the app and type-check its TSX, and *.test.tsx files beside it, written with nsgo/test , run with its Go tests.
Beside the package, nsgo.yaml names the app and its targets:
Beside nsgo.yaml , resources/ holds files the app ships, where asset: images load from and nsgo.Fonts("fonts/Brand.ttf") registers fonts from; assets/ holds project files that do not ship, such as the icons.
Add the tool to your module once; go tool nsgo then runs it without installing:
go tool nsgo dev runs the app once, or with dev.hot_reload rebuilds and restarts it on each change; a change of TSX alone updates the running app in place, keeping the state of what did not change. A failed build shows over the running app; Command or Control+R in the app, or r and Return in the terminal, builds it again. -trace prints each of the running app's commits, its time and mount items, on every target.
go tool nsgo build writes a stripped release package per target: an .app , an .ipa , an .apk , Windows' and Linux's directories, or a web site. -run starts the one built for this machine, or installs it on an iPhone, simulator or Android device, which -device picks.
-embed packages the app for an iOS or Android app of your own instead: an XCFramework (of dynamic frameworks with -dynamic ) or an AAR whose NSGoView or NsgoView shows it. Go desktop programs show apps with nsgo.NewView , and web pages with the site's nsgo.js . The host is the page's, or the module nsgo.yaml 's web.host names. See examples/embed-* .
go tool nsgo test runs the app's tests, its *.test.tsx among them, with a line per test; -run filters them, -junit report.xml writes a JUnit report and -trace prints each step's mount items and commit times. -target runs them on macos , windows , linux , web (in Chrome, Chromium or Edge), ios_simulator or android , a process per test, saving screenshots in .nsgo/test/screenshots . build.targets and -target accept all for every platform that needs only Go and Xcode; add android_x64 when an NDK is installed.
Flags replace the nsgo.yaml values they name, such as -target , -version or -output ; dev and build take -device for an iPhone, simulator or Android device, build -team to sign the iPhone's package, and dev -port for its server. -h lists every flag.
On macOS, a scroll view's edge effects ( Scroll.EdgeEffects ) blur through Core Animation's private CABackdropLayer and CAFilter , as AppKit's own edge effects do, since no public API varies a blur across a view. Mac App Store review may reject apps that use private APIs: NSGo calls them only for scroll views with edge bars, but every macOS build contains their names.
Requirements: macOS with Xcode and Go 1.26 or later. Nothing else is needed to build every target for arm64, Android's APK included.
Android device and emulator development additionally needs adb from the Android SDK's platform-tools, and iOS device development needs an Apple ID in Xcode's Accounts, a trusted iPhone and Developer Mode on it.
The x86_64 emulator target, android_x64 , also needs an Android NDK: Go links android/amd64 only with cgo. On Windows, Go 1.26 or later runs the native app and builds the Windows and web packages. On Linux, Go runs the native app once GTK 4.14 or newer, Pango and Cairo are installed, WebKitGTK 6.0 for web views and GStreamer plug-ins for videos.
Run the gallery from the repository root: NSH's gallery in Go, a demo of each element, base component and service. A wide window shows the demos in a sidebar; a narrow one is a phone's index.
NSGo uses NSH as its reference implementation, and aligns with its releases. Clone it into nsh/ at the repository root and check out its latest release tag, never main ; Git ignores that directory:
Read ARCHITECTURE.md and AGENTS.md before changing code.
The website at https://oneo-me.github.io/nsgo/ is a React home page whose live gallery runs the gallery's WebAssembly build. Run it from website/ with bun install and bun run dev , or build it with bun run build ; the Website workflow publishes website/dist to GitHub Pages. The website needs Bun 1.4 or later.
